title: The project hub exists at v17 in folder 14 Story Updates while the realignment writes v15 in folder 12 Project communication
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Document Control Sheet v12.xlsx (row 116, project hub); 14 Story Updates/Recovery Workbench Project Hub v15.html, v16.html and v17.html; _work/msr/plan/docs.json (D2-HUB takes 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Project Hub v14.html and writes v15)
section: Source document 116 (the project hub row of v12) and the new document 277 of v13
description: Row 116 of the source sheet already names Recovery Workbench Project Hub v17.html in folder 14 Story Updates and its comment says version 17 is the ACE re-base plus D-RCV-36 with 331 live stories. The realignment work package D2-HUB takes the v14 file in folder 12 Project communication as its source and writes v15 beside it, so the newest realignment file carries a lower number than a file that already exists in another folder, and two different files both sit at or above v15 without a stated order between them.
evidence: v12 Control sheet row 116 Files cell 'Recovery Workbench Project Hub v17.html' and comment 'Version 17 is the ACE re-base plus D-RCV-36: 331 live stories...'; folder 14 Story Updates holds Project Hub v15.html, v16.html and v17.html; folder 12 Project communication holds Project Hub v14.html and the new v15.html; Template and Rules v1 R8.2 says the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1 in the same folder
proposed: Keep both rows in this sheet, and when the two hub families are merged into one location renumber the realignment hub to the next number above v17 and record the renumbering in the change log of that file

title: The control sheet has no owner column, so the owning service can only be carried in the comments column
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Document Control Sheet v12.xlsx (columns A to K); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (Services sheet)
section: Control sheet header row and every added row
description: The work package says to use the Ownership Map for every owner, but the control sheet has 11 columns and none of them is an owner: it names reviewed-by and signed-off-by roles only. The Ownership Map holds the owning service per table, endpoint, event, workflow and job, and a service per code, not a document owner. The v13 rows therefore name the owning service in the comments column and do not add a twelfth column, which would have changed the header and every one of the 134 source rows.
evidence: Header row A4:K4 of the source sheet: #, Priority, Layer, Document, Files, Reviewed by, Signed off by, Uploaded on, Review status, Signed off on, Comments and missing items; Ownership Map Services sheet columns Code, Service, Name, Wave, Schema, REST base, Topic, Queue
proposed: Add an Owner column in a later version of the sheet if the register is to be read without the comment text, and fill it from the Ownership Map where the document belongs to one service

title: 'One row per new file' does not fit the document granularity the 134 source rows use for the 1065 story files
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Document Control Sheet v12.xlsx (rows 52, 55 and 109); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/ (1065 files in 31 epic folders); _work/msr/wp/D2-CTL.md
description: The work package asks for one row per new file. The source sheet controls documents, not files: row 52 already lists three files on one row (a story-file zip, a .md and an .xlsx), and the new story set holds 1065 story files in 31 epic folders against 134 source rows. The v13 sheet keeps the document convention and controls the story files as 31 rows, one per epic folder, with the file count in the Files cell; a folder family such as the functional specifications v7, the technical specifications v6, the API specification v5 or the physical schema v7 is one row with its file count. The result is 161 added rows: 85 rows that continue an existing family and 76 for documents that are new in v15.
evidence: v12 row 52 Files cell lists 'Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7.zip, Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 v9.md, Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 v9.xlsx'; 1065 files under 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1 in 31 folders; Functional Specifications by Module v7 holds 38 files, Technical Specifications by Module v6 holds 39, API Specification v5 holds 41, Physical Schema v7 holds 21
proposed: If a per-file register is needed, take it from the Document Index v14 or from the work package edit logs and keep this sheet at document level

title: The document index v14 was not in the tree when the control sheet of the set was written
source: 12 Project communication/ (folder listing at 23 November 2026); _work/msr/wp/queue-D.json (the D2-IDX work package writes Recovery Workbench Document Index v14.md)
section: New row for the document index (document 275 of v13)
description: The control sheet is the register of the whole document set, so it carries a row for every realignment document including the ones other work packages issue at the same time. The project hub v15, the team start pack v3 and the CTO presentation v4 were in the tree when this sheet was written; the document index v14 was not, because its work package had not been run yet. The row is carried with Review status 'Not started' and the comments column records that the file was not yet in the tree; no other value of that row is invented.
evidence: Folder 12 Project communication at 23 November 2026 holds Document Index v13.md as the highest version, and holds Project Hub v15.html, Team Start Pack v3.pptx, Executive Presentation CTO v4.pptx and Project Overview v5.pptx from this run; queue-D.json lists 'Recovery Workbench Document Index v14.md' as the expected output of D2-IDX
proposed: Set the review status of the row when the document index v14 is issued, and confirm the file name in the Files cell against it

title: The Summary formulas of v12 counted rows 5 to 136 only, so documents 133 and 134 were never counted
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Document Control Sheet v12.xlsx (Summary sheet formulas; Control sheet rows 5 to 138)
description: Every count on the Summary sheet reads 'Control sheet'!$B$5:$B$136 and the same range for the review status column, while the control sheet carries 134 documents in rows 5 to 138. The two documents added in v12, the Temporal and Drools change register (133) and Rule story retirements (134), fall outside the range and are not counted in any priority band. The realignment needed the range to reach the new last row in any case, so v13 sets every Summary formula to rows 5 to 299.
evidence: v12 Summary B5 '=COUNTIF('Control sheet'!$B$5:$B$136,A5)'; Control sheet max row 138 with document 134 at row 138; v13 Summary B5 reads '$B$5:$B$299' and the control sheet ends at row 299
proposed: Keep the range a named range or a whole-column reference so it cannot fall behind the control sheet again

title: No source states the priority, the layer or the review roles of a document that is new in v15
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Document Control Sheet v12.xlsx (Key sheet: what each priority and status means); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: The 76 added rows for new documents
description: Seventy-six of the added rows are documents that have no earlier row: the BRD for Epics 3 to 8, twenty PRDs, the service story catalog, the service epics file, 31 story-file folders, the service catalog, the service template specification, the service contract catalog, the Kafka topic and event catalog, the Temporal workflow and activity catalog, the integration test plan, the Day-1 work allocation, the service epic diagrams, twelve rows of run material and the two registers. For these the priority band, the layer and the reviewed-by and signed-off-by roles are copied from the nearest existing family: platform and contract material from the technical rows, new requirements from the BRD rows, story sets from the story rows, the registers and run material from the control rows. No source states a priority or a reviewer for a document that did not exist before v15.
evidence: Key sheet defines three priority bands and five review statuses and says nothing about how a new document is placed; the source rows carry reviewers by family, for example 'Data architect, recovery tech lead, ACE team lead' for the change register and 'SCB IT architecture, ACE team, TechX' for the architecture rows; Ownership Map Services and Rulings sheets name owning services and rulings, not document reviewers
proposed: Confirm the band and the reviewer of each new document at the first review of the set, and record any change in the next version of this sheet
